statement.p: Find the Jacobian. \frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}, where x = 5s-t-3u, y = 2t-5s-4u, z = 3t-3s-5u.

static.solution: \left|\frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}\right| = \left|\begin{array}{ccc} x_s \amp x_t \amp x_u\\ y_s \amp y_t \amp y_u\\ z_s \amp z_t \amp z_u \end{array}\right| =\left|\begin{array}{ccc} 5 \amp -1 \amp -3\\ -5 \amp 2 \amp -4\\ -3 \amp 3 \amp -5 \end{array}\right|. This 3 \times 3 determinant is computed the same way as for the cross product, with the entries 5,-1,-3 in the first row playing the same role as \vec i,\vec j,\vec k. We get \frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}= ((2)(-5)-(-4)(3))5 + ((-4)(-3)-(-5)(-5))-1 + ((-5)(3)-(2)(-3))-3 = 50.
